summary.intent: Autonomously run the full post-execute-phase ship pipeline for GSD Phase 68 (verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK E2E gate, CodeRabbit review, ship, resolve PR reviews) without stopping for user input except on real failures or the final merge decision.
summary.outcome: Verify was accepted from existing PASS artifacts; secure-phase and validate-phase audits ran and updated SECURITY.md/VALIDATION.md (0 gaps, unit suites green); simplify review found and fixed a real zeroization-order bug in client.ts (with a new regression test) plus dead code in two web files; commit-reword step was a no-op since all 86 commits were already conventional; SDK E2E gate required rebuilding a stale TEE worker container to get valid results; three todos were filed for deferred/pre-existing issues (web vitest not wired into CI, a dead SDK share-scaffolding path, and a refresh-access path with no live trigger); ship/CodeRabbit/PR-review steps had not yet completed by the end of the captured transcript.

repo: In this repo's commitlint/lint-pr-title rules, scoped parens like `feat(68-03):` are valid — the 'no parentheses' rule only applies to the description text, not the conventional-commit scope syntax. A prior assumption that all `feat 68-03:`-style subjects needed rewording was wrong; grep over `git log` showed all 86 commits already conformed.

The tee-worker container used for local SDK E2E runs can silently run stale code — it had to be rebuilt and restarted from current source before the republish/renewal tests reflected the actual client.ts logic.

apps/web unit tests (vitest) are not actually invoked by any CI job in ci.yml — a failing test (ipns.service.test) can exist on `main` itself with no CI signal catching it, since nothing runs `pnpm --filter web test` in the pipeline.

SDK E2E suite exiting 0 doesn't guarantee full coverage — some suites skip conditionally (e.g. TEE-dependent tests) and the skip reasons must be checked in the raw output, not inferred from the exit code.

code.finding: Zeroization-order bug: sensitive key material was being zeroized before enumerateMoveDescendants finished using it during moveItem, causing incorrect enumeration; fixed by reordering zeroization after descendant enumeration.

Contained dead code (an unused `ensureFreshSentShares`-related scaffolding) with zero external importers — confirmed via grep before removal; flagged remaining unretired parts as a deferred todo rather than a full removal.
Contained a dead code path with no external references, removed as part of the simplify pass.

New regression test added for the moveItem/enumerateMoveDescendants zeroization-order bug; verified red (fails against the unfixed code) before confirming green with the fix, per red-green discipline.

workflow: When a suspicious test failure appears only on a feature branch, diff the exact file against `main` and, if structurally identical, do a decisive swap-in experiment (temporarily replace with main's version and re-run) rather than continuing to reason abstractly about mock/import chains.
Before removing suspected dead code, verify zero external references (grep across the repo) and re-check remaining in-file usages line-by-line before applying edits.

Background long-running jobs (security audit, simplify review, client-chain build, SDK E2E) run concurrently while the orchestrator continues other prep (PR/auth checks) — but full test suites should not be run concurrently across parallel subagents (memory: feedback-gsd-concurrent-suites-ram) since it can starve RAM.

friction: Diagnosing the ipns.service.test failure was a long detour — required tracing import chains, comparing mocks against main, checking CI job configs, and a swap-in experiment before concluding it was pre-existing and not even covered by CI.

SDK E2E gate initially looked fine (exit 0) but the TEE-related suites were silently skipping until the tee-worker container was rebuilt from current source — exit code alone was not a trustworthy signal.
Locating exact dead-code spans and confirming zero references required multiple rounds of grep/read before edits could be safely applied.
